items.title: Joseph 'One Eyed Babe' Phillips Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: And that daddy died. Up there in Natchez. He left property for his wife, Cheryl Lucille. And he left property for her.

ctx.x: No, Punch is here. He's staying at the Page Hotel. Oh, no. That's right. Oh. Punch is here? Yeah. I almost got arrested with another night. I had a headache so I didn't play. Oh. The judge didn't like it. We were mixing it up, you know. Yeah, I know they don't like it.

I almost got arrested with another night. They just don't like it. And it ain't no use of trying to put it over. They don't like it. And it's been going on before you, you, me or him was born. That mix. And they ain't gonna never break it up. Oh, no. Well, I mean, you just gotta sit in. They ain't gonna be friends. They ain't gonna never break that mess up, no, huh? I have a cousin, she might pass here. She's white as you, and no more as my cousin. She's kind of me. Yeah. That's right. And that daddy died. Up…

I thought the French was standing, it wasn't, I thought it was called the Lachs. It's a Page. I think it's a Page Hotel on that part. Not too far from here. No. But Eddie Morris is playing with him now. You remember Eddie Morris? The trombone player. Morris? Yeah. The trombone player was with him when he had Joe. Georgey Boyd and Johnny and all those fellows. Yeah. He comes back. What you got?
